title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not by Grothendieck. The header reads 'CORNU Philippe, 16 juin 1978, C4 Mathématiques' and the page is numbered I. It is the first page of a student report from a Montpellier course certificate (C4), apparently kept among Grothendieck's papers and filed in the Teichmüller dossier. The neighbouring pages are Grothendieck's own computations on P^1 minus {0,1,∞}: the map g(z)=(2z-1)^2, loops l_0, l_1, l_∞, and homomorphisms of the profinite π_{0,3}.

What the student does: take two stereographic projections of the spherical icosahedron, one centred at a face centre and one at an edge midpoint. The 15 great circles drawn are the 15 mirror planes of the icosahedral group (of order 120).
- Circles through the projection centre become straight lines, the 'circles with centre at infinity'. Two mirror planes pass through an edge midpoint, giving 2 lines; three pass through a face centre (the 3-fold axis), giving 3 lines.
- Edges: each mirror circle contains exactly 2 (opposite) edges, so there are 2×15 = 30 edges.
- Vertices: each circle contains 4 vertices, and each vertex (a 5-fold axis) lies on 5 mirror circles, so there are 4×15/5 = 12 vertices.
- Faces: each circle carries 2 edges, each bordered by 2 faces, giving 4 face–circle incidences per circle. Each face has 3 edges lying on 3 distinct circles, so there are 4×15/3 = 20 faces.
- The same configuration of circles also exhibits the dual dodecahedron.

This is a double-counting exercise on the icosahedral reflection arrangement. Its likely link to Grothendieck is his teaching of regular polyhedra and spherical tessellations at Montpellier around 1977-78. That teaching later feeds into dessins d'enfants and the triangle-group (2,3,5) picture, but nothing of that appears on this page.
errors: No mathematical errors. The counts 30/12/20, the 5 circles per vertex, and the 2 vs 3 straight lines in the two projections are all correct.

One wording imprecision: the 4 'face–circle incidences' per circle are counted through the 2 edges on the circle. The student's phrase 'de part et d'autre desquelles se trouvent une face' is loose but the count is right.

ideas.what: Counting vertices, edges and faces of the icosahedron by double counting incidences with the 15 mirror great circles seen in stereographic projection
ideas.modern_name: Icosahedral reflection arrangement (Coxeter group H3, 15 reflecting planes); incidence double counting

ideas.what: Visibility of the dual dodecahedron in the same circle arrangement
ideas.modern_name: Duality of regular polyhedra / common symmetry group A5×Z2

deep.surprise_reason: This is a student's routine counting exercise on the icosahedron (1978), not Grothendieck's mathematics. Its only interest is archival: it shows Grothendieck kept student work on regular polyhedra alongside his π_{0,3} computations.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is essentially correct. The page is authored by Philippe Cornu, a student, not by Grothendieck; the header 'CORNU Philippe 16 juin 1978, C4 Mathématiques' and the page number 'I' should be flagged accordingly.
